method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

items.assessment: Electrical mechanism with brief loss of consciousness supports internal/cardiac assessment despite small surface injury; this is a useful surface-versus-depth misconception.
The substance-specific instructions and PPE distinguish safe decontamination from familiar neutralization/covering errors; no universal irrigation rule is asserted.
Foundational local burn cooling item addresses recognizable ice, butter and whole-body cooling misconceptions while protecting a child from hypothermia.
Persistent low urine with verified catheter patency and new respiratory congestion test both inadequate perfusion and poor fluid tolerance rather than automatic fluid escalation.
Chest-wall restriction is a useful concern, but tighter dressing and oral fluid are weak alternatives against worsening ventilation.
issues: Chest-wall restriction is a useful concern, but tighter dressing and oral fluid are weak alternatives against worsening ventilation.
proposedChanges: Use parallel causes or relevant assessment findings: restrictive eschar, bronchospasm, retained secretions, or airway oedema with enough data to distinguish; application is more appropriate than challenge for simple recognition.

items.assessment: Staged exposure and active warming are coherent burn-care measures; evaporation and airflow alternatives test specific heat-loss mechanisms.
Pain-versus-depth concept is useful, but already-healed interpretation of a fresh leathery burn is implausible.
issues: Pain-versus-depth concept is useful, but already-healed interpretation of a fresh leathery burn is implausible.
proposedChanges: Replace with a credible depth-assessment misconception, or ask to compare documented tissue features and priorities rather than offering an obviously temporally impossible explanation.

items.assessment: Supporting prescribed rehab is sound, but forceful beyond-prescription stretching is a giveaway.
issues: Supporting prescribed rehab is sound, but forceful beyond-prescription stretching is a giveaway.
proposedChanges: Use plausible modification proposals such as shorter sessions, longer splint periods, prescribed analgesia timing, or therapist technique review; avoid independently prescribing a changed regimen.

items.assessment: The fat-embolism pattern is meaningful, but sleep and dermatology-review alternatives are remote from new hypoxaemia.
issues: The fat-embolism pattern is meaningful, but sleep and dermatology-review alternatives are remote from new hypoxaemia.
proposedChanges: Ask which clinical concern should be highlighted, comparing fat embolism, pulmonary thromboembolism, opioid-related hypoventilation and pneumonia using the timing/petechiae data.

items.assessment: Preserved pulse does not exclude compartment syndrome, but exercise-before-review and analgesia-until-sleep are conspicuous errors.
issues: Preserved pulse does not exclude compartment syndrome, but exercise-before-review and analgesia-until-sleep are conspicuous errors.
proposedChanges: Use parallel interpretations or plain relevant assessment actions; retain the specific stretch-pain/sensory pattern and avoid another generic urgent-call item.

items.assessment: New alignment change requires protection, but walking to test, rotating back and completing the transfer make every alternative cartoon unsafe.
issues: New alignment change requires protection, but walking to test, rotating back and completing the transfer make every alternative cartoon unsafe.
proposedChanges: Ask which findings distinguish suspected dislocation from postoperative pain, or compare supported-position, analgesia, neurovascular-assessment and urgent-contact actions with a clear first-physical-action boundary.

items.assessment: Observed weight-on-floor and changed positioning directly explain ineffective traction; restoring the prescribed mechanical setup is distinct from changing the force.
Infection plus loosening is relevant, but tightening hardware and next-week review make the key obvious.
issues: Infection plus loosening is relevant, but tightening hardware and next-week review make the key obvious.
proposedChanges: Use parallel clinical concerns or credible initial actions such as assessing drainage, checking neurovascular status, following current site-care orders, and requesting fixation review.

items.assessment: Treatment endpoint teaching is correct but mostly generic antimicrobial adherence; saving leftovers and taking on painful days are weak.
issues: Treatment endpoint teaching is correct but mostly generic antimicrobial adherence; saving leftovers and taking on painful days are weak.
proposedChanges: Create a bone-infection-specific follow-up problem involving symptom improvement with a remaining prescribed course and an adverse effect or administration barrier, requiring appropriate review rather than generic adherence repetition.

items.assessment: Febrile non-weight-bearing child requires review, but exercise/sprain-delay/routine-physio alternatives are weak.
issues: Febrile non-weight-bearing child requires review, but exercise/sprain-delay/routine-physio alternatives are weak.
proposedChanges: Use parallel concerns such as septic arthritis, transient synovitis, minor injury and osteomyelitis, with sufficient findings and a question about the concern requiring exclusion rather than independent diagnosis.

items.assessment: New motor/sensory deficit is meaningful; discharge delay and wound-pain normalization telegraph wrong answers.
issues: New motor/sensory deficit is meaningful; discharge delay and wound-pain normalization telegraph wrong answers.
proposedChanges: Use focused neurovascular findings or a comparison of nerve compression, pain-limited movement and deconditioning; preserve documented baseline change.

items.assessment: This substantially duplicates current x-basic-179 phantom-pain acknowledgement and assessment.
issues: This substantially duplicates current x-basic-179 phantom-pain acknowledgement and assessment.
proposedChanges: Replace with a distinct task such as evaluating response to an established phantom-pain plan or distinguishing a new residual-limb problem during prosthesis use; do not repeat recognition-and-validation.

items.assessment: The new perfusion findings should override phantom-pain anchoring, but heating-pad-before-contact adds a conspicuous unsafe option.
issues: The new perfusion findings should override phantom-pain anchoring, but heating-pad-before-contact adds a conspicuous unsafe option.
proposedChanges: Use a plausible residual-limb assessment or existing pain-plan action in place of heating; remove artificial before/after delays and explain the tissue evidence.

items.assessment: Step count and appointment count are unrelated filler, so no neurovascular reasoning is required.
issues: Step count and appointment count are unrelated filler, so no neurovascular reasoning is required.
proposedChanges: Use plausible limb-assessment alternatives such as local bruising/tenderness and proximal range of motion; ask specifically for distal neurovascular comparisons, or give pre/post findings requiring interpretation.

items.assessment: Walker-part names and a signed sheet despite no transfer are weak process distractors.
issues: Walker-part names and a signed sheet despite no transfer are weak process distractors.
proposedChanges: Compare concrete functional changes such as assistance level, balance, pain tolerance, speed, fatigue or distance; define the safe-transfer goal clearly enough that only the intended outcomes satisfy it.

items.assessment: Heat-stroke response is correct, but large oral drinks despite stated swallowing impairment and a distant walk make alternatives too easy.
issues: Heat-stroke response is correct, but large oral drinks despite stated swallowing impairment and a distant walk make alternatives too easy.
proposedChanges: Compare plausible first-aid plans including local cooling methods, cooling during emergency activation, or shaded rest with close reassessment; preserve rapid cooling and emergency response without unnecessary bundled-key length.

items.assessment: Stopping shivering despite continued wet/cold exposure plus neurological change supports worsening hypothermia; the interpretation corrects a recognizable false-recovery cue.
Rubbing and uncontrolled direct heat are common harmful rewarming misconceptions; controlled rewarming with no refreezing risk and protection are explicitly contextualized.
Respiratory symptoms after submersion need evaluation, but large meal and face-down draining are weak choices against increasing fatigue.
issues: Respiratory symptoms after submersion need evaluation, but large meal and face-down draining are weak choices against increasing fatigue.
proposedChanges: Use competing interpretations of persistent cough/tachypnoea after submersion or concrete monitoring/escalation plans, avoiding unsafe folklore as the bulk of the option set.

items.assessment: Incomplete physiological recovery is correct, but anxiety and discharge-with-confusion alternatives are weak.
issues: Incomplete physiological recovery is correct, but anxiety and discharge-with-confusion alternatives are weak.
proposedChanges: Ask which trend best demonstrates recovery using core temperature, cognition, pulse and urine/perfusion data; distinguish skin cooling from systemic response with comparable data clusters.
